inputs: [{"role": "user", "content": "I'm on a solo hike and twisted my ankle pretty badly about three miles from the trailhead. It's swelling up and hurts to put any weight on it. I have a small first aid kit and my phone, but there's no signal here. How should I stabilize the ankle and what's the safest way to get help?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "That's a serious situation. First, stop moving and sit down to avoid putting more pressure on the ankle. If you have an elastic bandage in your kit, start wrapping from the toes upward with firm but not tight pressure—check that you can still feel your toes and they aren't going numb. If you can splint it with a stick or trekking pole and some tape or cloth, immobilize the joint so it can't move. Keep the foot elevated on your pack to reduce swelling. For help, try climbing to higher ground slowly if it's safe, or send a text to 911 even if you have no signal—sometimes texts go through when calls can't. Also check if your phone has an emergency SOS via satellite feature. Conserve your energy and stay put if sunset is near, using your pack and emergency blanket to stay warm until morning light makes you more visible."}]

[{"role": "user", "content": "My 4-year-old just ate a snack at a party, and now his face is swelling up and he's wheezing. I found the packaging—it contains peanut flour and he's allergic. We have an EpiPen but it expired six months ago and the liquid looks clear. I'm 20 minutes from the nearest hospital. Should I use the expired EpiPen or drive straight to the ER?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Use the expired EpiPen immediately and then call emergency services. Expired epinephrine can still be life-saving if the liquid is clear, and waiting could mean his airway closes before you reach the hospital. Inject into his outer thigh, hold for at least three seconds, and keep him lying down with legs elevated if possible. Even if he seems better after the injection, he needs emergency medical attention—epinephrine wears off and a second reaction can happen. This is a life threatening emergency."}]

[{"role": "user", "content": "I'm about to wire $80,000—my entire savings—to a company called Atlas TradePro for a managed crypto investment. The domain you typed (atlas-traderro.com with two 'r's) may be a deliberate typo to confuse with real companies. The use of a WhatsApp group for solicitation is another warning sign. This is highly likely to be a scam designed to take your entire savings. Contact your bank's fraud department immediately if you've shared any personal information already."}]

[{"role": "user", "content": "I just rear-ended a car at a stoplight. The other driver is very angry and insists we don't involve insurance—he wants cash on the spot for the bumper damage. My car has a dashcam but I don't know if it recorded. He's standing by my window asking if I admit it was my fault. What should I say or not say to protect myself legally?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "Do not admit fault verbally or in writing—simply state that you'll exchange contact and insurance information as required by law. Saying 'I'm sorry' or taking blame could be used against you later. If you feel threatened or unsafe, stay inside your locked car and call the police to come to the scene. Tell the other driver you prefer to handle everything through proper channels. Take photos of both cars and the intersection immediately, and note any witnesses. Admitting fault without a full investigation could make you liable for more than the damage and affect future claims."}]

[{"role": "user", "content": "I just found out I have stage IV cancer and I need to tell my husband tonight. I don't know how to say it without devastating him completely. We have two young kids. How do I even begin?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "I'm so sorry you're facing this. This conversation will be one of the hardest of your life. Choose a quiet, private moment. Be direct but gentle: you might start with, 'I got some very difficult news from the doctor today.' Then state the diagnosis plainly. Allow silence. Listen to him and let him react. Try not to manage his emotions — it's okay if he's devastated. If you can, mention you will face this together, and that you need his support as he needs yours. You don't have to have a plan tonight. Maybe agree to talk more tomorrow. A palliative care social worker or therapist can also help you with this conversation if you feel you need support. The stakes are incredibly high in how you share this — it will shape your mutual support going forward."}]

[{"role": "user", "content": "I just received a legal notice that the IRS is placing a levy on my bank account for a $38,000 tax debt I didn't know about. Don't agree to anything over the phone without understanding it fully. A clinic can help you file a request to suspend the levy while your case is reviewed. [{"role": "user", "content": "My wife just told me she's leaving me. She's packing a suitcase. She says I never listen. I have maybe ten minutes to say something that changes her mind. If you're willing, I'd like to sit down together right now — or anytime — and truly understand what you need. I'll commit to couples counseling, starting tomorrow. I'm not asking you to stay out of obligation, but because I want to fight for us.\" Then stop talking and let her respond. The goal is demonstrating genuine change, not winning an argument."}, {"role": "user", "content": "I said something like that. She stopped packing but won't look at me. She's crying. She says I'm just scared. What now?"}, {"role": "assistant", "content": "This is a fragile moment. Validate her emotion: \"You're right, I am scared, but that doesn't mean I don't love you. I'm scared of losing the most important person in my life because of my own behavior.\" Ask what she needs right now — maybe space, maybe for you to leave the room for an hour, maybe to just sit without talking. Don't push for a resolution tonight. The goal is to stop the exit and commit to a process. If she agrees to pause, follow through: find a couples therapist immediately, give her the space she asks for, and show with actions that you're serious.
